input.command:
cd <WORKTREE>
for f in sources/*.md; do
  n=$(basename "$f" .md | sed 's/source-//')
  # regions mentioned in this file
  regs=$(grep -oE '^Region [0-9]+' "$f" | sort -u | tr '\n' ',')
  batches=$(grep -cE '^## Batch [0-9]+$' "$f")
  seq_ok=$(grep -oE '^## Batch [0-9]+$' "$f" | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | sort -n | uniq | tr '\n' ' ' | md5)
  expect=$(seq 1 30 | sort -n | tr '\n' ' ' | md5)
  lbl=$(grep -oE 'audit label is R[0-9]+-B[0-9]+' "$f" | grep -coE "R${n}-B")
  echo "$f region=[$regs] batches=$batches seq_match=$([ "$seq_ok" = "$expect" ] && echo yes || echo NO) labels_matching_R${n}=$lbl"
done
echo "--- line accounting (blank + headings + bodies + residual == total) ---"
for f in sources/*.md; do
  t=$(wc -l < "$f"); b=$(grep -cE '^$' "$f"); h=$(grep -cE '^## Batch [0-9]+$' "$f")
  y=$(grep -cE '^Region [0-9]+ processes batch' "$f"); r=4
  echo "$(basename $f) total=$t blank=$b head=$h body=$y residual=$r sum=$((b+h+y+r))"
done

# READING.md — coverage ledger and findings for `sources/`

Scope: all 12 files in `sources/`. Read-only review. No source was modified.

## 1. Coverage ledger

Coverage is complete and verifiable: **12/12 sources read, 0 failed, 0 not-yet-read**,
and **1140/1140 lines accounted for**.

| Source | Path | Lines | Status | Owner | Retention | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SRC-01 | `sources/source-01.md` | 95 | read | owner-01 | 14 days | L62 |
| SRC-02 | `sources/source-02.md` | 95 | read | owner-02 | 30 days | L62 |
| SRC-03 | `sources/source-03.md` | 95 | read | owner-03 | 14 days | L62 |
| SRC-04 | `sources/source-04.md` | 95 | read | owner-04 | 30 days | L62 |
| SRC-05 | `sources/source-05.md` | 95 | read | owner-05 | 14 days | L62 |
| SRC-06 | `sources/source-06.md` | 95 | read | owner-06 | 30 days | L62 |
| SRC-07 | `sources/source-07.md` | 95 | read | owner-07 | 14 days | L62 |
| SRC-08 | `sources/source-08.md` | 95 | read | owner-08 | 30 days | L62 |
| SRC-09 | `sources/source-09.md` | 95 | read | owner-09 | 14 days | L62 |
| SRC-10 | `sources/source-10.md` | 95 | read | owner-10 | 30 days | L62 |
| SRC-11 | `sources/source-11.md` | 95 | read | owner-11 | 14 days | L62 |
| SRC-12 | `sources/source-12.md` | 95 | read | owner-12 | 30 days | L62 |

### Method, and why it supports the coverage claim

The corpus is highly repetitive: each file is one region's review, built from 30
near-identical "Batch" sections plus four distinctive lines. Rather than assert
coverage from a skim, every line was classified deterministically:

- `source-01.md` was read in full, directly, to establish the document shape.
- For all 12 files, every line was matched against the boilerplate batch pattern.
  Lines that did **not** match were printed in full and read individually — 4 per
  file, 48 in total (title, `Source ID`, `Status`, and the owner/retention line).
- Line accounting per file: 31 blank + 30 batch headings + 30 batch bodies + 4
  distinctive lines = 95 lines. This holds for all 12 files, so no line went unread
  or unclassified.
- The boilerplate itself was checked for hidden variation rather than assumed
  uniform: each file references exactly one region matching its filename, contains
  batches 1–30 with no gaps or duplicates, and carries 30 audit labels all matching
  that file's own region prefix (`R01-B*` … `R12-B*`).
- All 12 files are byte-distinct (SHA-256 verified), so none is a duplicate.

No delegation was used. The distinctive material is 48 lines; splitting it across
workers would have cost more than reading it and added an unnecessary layer between
the findings and their sources.

## 2. Owners

Each source names exactly one owner for exactly one region, and describes that
owner as unique for the region:

> "The unique region owner is owner-01." — `sources/source-01.md:62`

The mapping is one-to-one and consistent across the corpus: region *NN* → `owner-NN`,
for regions 01 through 12 (`sources/source-01.md:62` … `sources/source-12.md:62`).
No region is claimed by two owners, and no owner is claimed for two regions.

**There is no ownership conflict in this corpus.**

## 3. Retention

Two retention values appear, each stated with identical phrasing and identical
qualification:

- **14 days** — SRC-01, 03, 05, 07, 09, 11 (odd-numbered sources), e.g.
  `sources/source-01.md:62`: "Retention is 14 days."
- **30 days** — SRC-02, 04, 06, 08, 10, 12 (even-numbered sources), e.g.
  `sources/source-02.md:62`: "Retention is 30 days."

The split is exactly 6 / 6 and aligns perfectly with odd/even source numbering.
That regularity is a property of the corpus worth flagging — it may indicate a
generated fixture, two drafting batches, or a genuine regional difference. The
sources themselves give no reason for the pattern.

Every source qualifies its own value identically:

> "This value requires confirmation before implementation." — `sources/source-01.md:62`

So **no source presents its retention value as confirmed or implementable.**

## 4. Conflict — stated, not resolved

As instructed, I have not selected a policy. Here is the conflict and, importantly,
the open question that determines whether it *is* one.

**The disagreement:** six sources say 14 days, six say 30 days
(`sources/source-01.md:62` vs `sources/source-02.md:62`, and so on).

**The question the sources do not answer:** whether retention is scoped *per region*
or *organisation-wide*. Each statement appears inside a single region's review and
sits immediately after that region's owner, but no source says whether the value
binds only its own region or the whole estate.

- If retention is **per-region**, there is no contradiction. Region 01 retains for
  14 days and region 02 for 30, and all 12 statements are simultaneously true.
- If retention is **organisation-wide**, the corpus is directly self-contradictory
  and at most one group of six can be correct.

I could not resolve this from the material, and resolving it is a policy decision
rather than a reading one. It is the first thing to settle, because it decides
